findings.title: Three architecture-preview deferrals are asserted on a row D-002 keeps INSIDE the slice, in the wrong instrument, with no owner and no cited disposition — routing around the D-096 (A) bar that blocks every sibling deferral.
measured: D-002 'Condition-2 affected-row set under this slice' enumerates DR-127 explicitly. DR-127 is IN the slice.

D-002's explicit-deferral list is enumerated and closed: DR-108, DR-110, DR-116, DR-128, DR-129, Windows platform support, baseline/ratchet (conditional), and DR-106/DR-109/DR-113 each deferred WHOLLY. DR-127 does not appear. The list is prefaced 'Explicit deferrals (each gets its recorded disposition, never silence)'.

D-002 further binds: 'Each scoped inclusion elsewhere in this entry ... is likewise recorded as a scope disposition with its own artifact and commit when executed, so no scope exists only inside this register entry (turn-1 NOTE-10).'

The house instrument for preview deferral is documentClass SLICE-DEFERRAL-CANDIDATE (deferral.DR-108/110/116/106-109-113/windows .preview.v2.json), which carries ownerWhoMustRecord, scope ('architecture preview (D-002 / D-018) only'), commission, whatMustNotBePretendedSettled, and condition2EffectIfOwnerRecorded.

D-096 recorded those five candidates but held owner-recording blocked pending (A) an owner grant and (B) reviewed mechanics. D-097 withdrew the composed grant: 'Adopt nothing as D-096 (A). D-096 (A) remains unsatisfied.' D-100 supplied (B) only and states 'Mechanics alone never grants', with eligible candidates 'the five D-096 artifacts only'.

The subject is documentClass DESIGN-CONTRACT-CANDIDATE and carries previewDeferredPairs as three bare strings: 'Rust provider major 2', 'third-party / untrusted roles', 'authoritative evidence/replay format skew (DR-113)'. No ownerWhoMustRecord. No scope limit to architecture preview. No condition2EffectIfOwnerRecorded. No D-002 citation for any of the three. whatThisDoesNotDo never denies that these defer DR-127 preview scope.
findings.whyItIsABlocker: DR-127's row cell requires 'Bidirectional N/N+1 skew, independent rollback/coexistence'. previewDeferredPairs narrows that scope by removing the Rust provider surface, untrusted roles, and evidence-format skew. Two of the three do have a defensible slice basis in D-002 (language roles 'TypeScript, alone'; components 'first-party/explicitly-trusted only') and the third (DR-113) is genuinely deferred wholly by MF-03 — but the subject cites none of them. The defect is the route, not necessarily the substance: a coordinator recording this artifact as DR-127's accepted design contract would carry three preview-scope deferrals that no owner deferred, on a row D-002 places in the slice, inside an instrument that is not subject to the deferral bar. That is precisely the scope-by-silence D-002 forbids and precisely the owner path D-097 left unsatisfied.
findings.whatWouldClearIt: Either (a) delete previewDeferredPairs from this contract and route each item through its own SLICE-DEFERRAL-CANDIDATE with a named ownerWhoMustRecord, or (b) keep the field but convert each entry to a citation of the disposition that already owns it (D-002 language-roles / components clauses; MF-03 for DR-113) and state on the field that it records no new deferral, defers nothing itself, and that any DR-127 preview deferral still requires D-096 (A) plus D-100 mechanics.

findings.title: The row's entire preview scope is one line that mixes control-plane and provider-plane version vocabulary, and under its plain reading demands a control-protocol N+1 that the subject's own recorded input forecloses — reintroducing the same-version coupling this row exists to forbid.
measured: Subject, in full: 'distribution core + TypeScript component + control major 1, each at N and N+1 as independently qualified bytes.'

control-protocol-contract.v2 (governingSources[2]) .handshake.ownVersionSurface: 'proposed controlProtocolMajor = 1 ... It is its own DR-111 compatibility-matrix row ... NEVER a shared version with either provider protocol, the distribution core, or any component release. TypeScript provider major 1 and Rust provider major 2 are versions of THEIR surfaces; the numeric coincidence with controlMajor 1 carries no meaning and no coupling (file 02: There is no required same-version coupling).'

Same artifact, .compatibilityMatrixRow: 'supported readers = major 1 exactly (no cross-major window exists yet, and none can exist before a second major does); future-major refusal = typed via the frozen refusal core (RF-1), never best-effort parse; downgrade/no-return = no in-channel downgrade path exists (RF-8)'.
Same artifact: 'majors are the only compatibility unit' — there is no minor-version concept on the wire.
previewDeferredPairs[0] names 'Rust provider major 2' — a PROVIDER major — in the adjacent field to previewRequiredPairs' 'control major 1', a CONTROL major.
findings.whyItIsABlocker: Both available readings are defective. (a) If the quantifier 'each at N and N+1' distributes over all three named surfaces, the preview requires a control-protocol N+1, i.e. controlProtocolMajor 2. The consumed contract says no second control major exists, no cross-major window can exist before one does, and a future-major hello is refused TYPED via the frozen refusal core rather than interoperating. The preview is then unexecutable as written; worse, requiring core, component and control to step N->N+1 together is a same-version coupling across three surfaces that file 02 forbids and that DR-127 exists to prevent — a lockstep gate entering the anti-lockstep contract through its own scope line. (b) If the quantifier covers only the core and the component, with control pinned at major 1, then the control surface is silently excluded from the row cell's first requirement, 'Bidirectional N/N+1 skew', and the subject records that exclusion nowhere. The artifact does not say which reading is meant, and this single line is the whole of the row's proposed preview scope. The adjacent provider-major/control-major mixing is the same defect surfacing twice, in exactly the place the recorded input warns the numeric coincidence carries no meaning.
findings.whatWouldClearIt: Name the surfaces separately and bind the quantifier to each: state which surfaces move N->N+1 in the preview and which are pinned; if the control protocol is pinned at controlProtocolMajor 1 because no second major exists, say so and cite control-protocol-contract.v2 .compatibilityMatrixRow; and state explicitly that no surface's N+1 step is conditioned on any other surface stepping.
